title: Remote Reading Software for Radiologists | AuraPACS
meta: Remote reading software that lets your own radiologist read from home or a second site in a browser, with role-based access and every view audited.
h1: Remote reading software for your own radiologist, from home or a second site.
sub: AuraPACS gives the radiologist you already work with a browser viewer and reporting from anywhere you allow. Studies sync from the on-premise node through the cloud layer; the reader opens them, reports and signs. It is your radiologist, your archive and your report, not a pay-per-scan service.
whatsapp_text: Hi, our radiologist reads remotely and we'd like to discuss AuraPACS.
persona: Centre owner whose radiologist visits on set days or reads from another city, and who wants reporting to continue between visits

sections.h2: What remote reading means in AuraPACS
paras: Remote reading in AuraPACS means an authorised radiologist opens the centre's studies in a browser from wherever they are, scrolls the slices, adjusts window/level, writes the report on a template and signs it, exactly as they would in the reading room. Studies are received on the on-premise node and made available outside through the cloud layer.

This is teleradiology in the sense of reading at a distance, but it is not a teleradiology service. AuraPACS does not supply radiologists or charge per study read. It gives the radiologist you already work with a way to report between visits, and gives you role-based control and an audit trail over who saw what.

sections.eyebrow: Why remote reading is hard today
sections.h2: The radiologist is willing. The setup is what fails.
sections.lead: Most small centres have a radiologist who could read from home. What they lack is a safe way to get the study to them.

items.p: A few slices are photographed and sent; the radiologist reports on a fraction of the study.
A workstation client and a VPN that someone has to maintain, and that breaks when the radiologist changes laptop.
A shared login means nobody knows who opened which patient's study.
The document is emailed to the centre, printed and filed, disconnected from the images.
Outsourcing to a service solves the reading but bills every study forever and takes the relationship with your radiologist away.
Uploading a whole MR to a remote workstation over a weak line takes longer than the read.

sections.h2: Reading at a distance, three ways.

items.a: No. It does not supply radiologists or charge per study read. It gives your own radiologist a browser viewer and reporting from anywhere you allow. If you use a third-party reporting service as well, that is a separate arrangement.

items.q: What does the radiologist need at home?
items.a: A laptop with a standard browser and an internet connection. The viewer opens CT, MR, X-ray and ultrasound with nothing installed. Display quality for reading is the radiologist's choice.
Each radiologist has their own login with the radiologist role. Every view is audited, so the owner can see who opened which study and when. See radiology workflow.

items.q: Does the whole study have to upload before reading?
items.a: Studies sync from the on-premise node to the cloud layer in the background after they are received. The remote reader opens the synced study in the browser; on-site reading is never held up by the sync.

items.q: Can one radiologist cover two branches?
items.a: Yes. Each branch runs its own node and both sync to the cloud layer, so the reader sees a single pending list across sites.

items.q: Does the report written remotely reach the centre?
items.a: It is written on the study itself, so it is already at the centre the moment it is signed. Front desk sends the secure link on WhatsApp. See reporting software.
